In mathematics, especially in [[topology]], a '''Kuranishi structure''' is a smooth analogue of [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]] structure. If a topological space is endowed with a Kuranishi structure, then locally it can be identified with the zero set of a smooth map <math> (f_1, \ldots, f_k)\colon \R^{n+k} \to \R^k</math>, or the quotient of such a zero set by a finite group. Kuranishi structures were introduced by Japanese mathematicians [[Kenji Fukaya]] and Kaoru Ono in the study of [[Gromov–Witten invariants]] and [[Floer homology]] in [[symplectic geometry]], and were named after [[Masatake Kuranishi]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fukaya |first1=Kenji |author1-link=Kenji Fukaya| last2=Ono |first2=Kaoru |title=Arnold Conjecture and Gromov–Witten Invariant |journal=[[Topology (journal)|Topology]] |volume=38 |year=1999 |issue=5 |pages=933–1048 |doi=10.1016/S0040-9383(98)00042-1 |doi-access=|mr=1688434 }}</ref>

==Definition==

Let <math>X</math> be a [[Compact space|compact]] [[metrizable]] [[topological space]]. Let <math>p \in X</math> be a point. A '''Kuranishi neighborhood''' of <math>p</math> (of dimension <math>k</math>) is a 5-tuple

:::<math> K_p = (U_p, E_p, S_p, F_p, \psi_p) </math>

where

* <math>U_p</math> is a smooth [[orbifold]];
* <math>E_p \to U_p</math> is a smooth orbifold [[vector bundle]];
* <math>S_p\colon U_p \to E_p</math> is a smooth section;
* <math>F_p</math> is an open neighborhood of <math> p </math>;
* <math>\psi_p\colon S_p^{-1}(0) \to F_p</math> is a [[homeomorphism]].

They should satisfy that <math>\dim U_p - \operatorname{rank} E_p = k</math>.

If <math>p, q \in X</math> and <math>K_p = (U_p, E_p, S_p, F_p, \psi_p)</math>, <math>K_q = (U_q, E_q, S_q, F_q, \psi_q)</math> are their Kuranishi neighborhoods respectively, then a '''coordinate change''' from <math>K_q</math> to <math>K_p</math> is a triple

:::<math>T_{pq} = (U_{pq}, \phi_{pq}, \hat\phi_{pq}),</math>

where

* <math>U_{pq} \subset U_q </math> is an open sub-orbifold;
* <math>\phi_{pq}\colon U_{pq} \to U_p </math> is an orbifold embedding;
* <math>\hat\phi_{pq}\colon E_q|_{U_{pq}} \to E_p </math> is an orbifold vector bundle embedding which covers <math>\phi_{pq}</math>.

In addition, these data must satisfy the following compatibility conditions:

* <math>S_p \circ \phi_{pq} = \hat\phi_{pq} \circ S_q|_{U_{pq}}</math>;
* <math>\psi_p \circ \phi_{pq}|_{S_q^{-1}(0) \cap U_{pq}} = \psi_q|_{S_q^{-1}(0)\cap U_{pq}}</math>.

A '''Kuranishi structure''' on <math>X</math> of dimension <math>k</math> is a collection

::: <math>\Big( \{ K_p = (U_p, E_p, S_p, F_p, \psi_p) \ |\ p \in X \},\ \{ T_{pq} = (U_{pq}, \phi_{pq}, \hat\phi_{pq} ) \ |\ p \in X,\ q \in F_p\} \Big),</math>

where

* <math>K_p</math> is a Kuranishi neighborhood of <math>p</math> of dimension <math>k</math>;
* <math>T_{pq}</math> is a coordinate change from <math>K_q</math> to <math>K_p</math>.

In addition, the coordinate changes must satisfy the '''cocycle condition''', namely, whenever <math>q\in F_p,\ r \in F_q</math>, we require

::: <math>\phi_{pq} \circ \phi_{qr} = \phi_{pr},\ \hat\phi_{pq} \circ \hat\phi_{qr} = \hat\phi_{pr}</math>

over the regions where both sides are defined.

==History==

In [[Gromov–Witten invariant|Gromov–Witten theory]], one needs to define integration over the moduli space of pseudoholomorphic curves <math>\overline{\mathcal M}_{g, n} (X, A)</math>.<ref>{{cite book|last1=McDuff|first1= Dusa |author1-link=Dusa McDuff| last2=Salamon|first2= Dietmar |title=''J''-holomorphic curves and symplectic topology|series=American Mathematical Society Colloquium Publications|volume= 52|publisher= [[American Mathematical Society]]|location= Providence, RI|year= 2004|isbn=0-8218-3485-1| mr=2045629|doi=10.1090/coll/052}}</ref> This moduli space is roughly the collection of maps <math>u</math> from a nodal [[Riemann surface]] with genus <math>g</math> and <math>n</math> marked points into a [[symplectic manifold]] <math>X</math>, such that each component satisfies the [[Cauchy–Riemann equations|Cauchy–Riemann equation]]

::: <math>\overline\partial_J u  = 0</math>.

If the moduli space is a smooth, compact, oriented manifold or orbifold, then the integration (or a [[fundamental class]]) can be defined. When the symplectic manifold <math>X</math> is '''semi-positive''', this is indeed the case (except for codimension 2 boundaries of the moduli space) if the [[almost complex structure]] <math>J</math> is perturbed generically. However, when <math>X</math> is not semi-positive (for example, a smooth [[projective variety]] with negative first Chern class), the moduli space may contain configurations for which one component is a multiple cover of a holomorphic sphere <math>u\colon S^2 \to X</math> whose intersection with the first [[Chern class]] of <math>X</math> is negative. Such configurations make the moduli space very singular so a fundamental class cannot be defined in the usual way.

The notion of Kuranishi structure was a way of defining a virtual fundamental cycle, which plays the same role as a fundamental cycle when the moduli space is cut out transversely. It was first used by Fukaya and Ono in defining the Gromov–Witten invariants and Floer homology, and was further developed when Fukaya, [[Yong-Geun Oh]], Hiroshi Ohta, and Ono studied [[Floer homology|Lagrangian intersection Floer theory]].<ref name="Fukaya">{{cite book | last1=Fukaya | first1=Kenji | author1-link=Kenji Fukaya| last2=Oh|first2=Yong-Geun| author2-link=Yong-Geun Oh|last3= Ohta|first3= Hiroshi|last4= Ono|first4= Kaoru|title=Lagrangian intersection floer theory: anomaly and obstruction, Part I and Part II | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] and International Press | publication-place=Providence, RI and Somerville, MA |series=AMS/IP Studies in Advanced Mathematics|volume= 46| year=2009 | isbn=978-0-8218-4836-4 | oclc=426147150 |mr=2553465}} {{MR|id=2548482}}</ref>
